result.title: Reconfiguring Procedural Knowledge for Compositional Robot Skill Adaptation
result.summary: General-purpose behavior models increasingly internalize broad procedural knowledge during training, making their adaptation to new goals and skill interfaces less a problem of learning entirely new behaviors than of reconfiguring existing competence. We study this capability as reconfigurability, the ability to realize new behaviors by cost-efficiently restructuring existing components and relations under sparse governing information, where task specifications provide high-level goals and procedure specifications expose a limited set of reusable factors, leaving the concrete bindings and compositions required for execution underdetermined. We propose RecPo, a framework that represents skills task-agnostically through multiple procedure views and materializes executable skill sequences by composing stored transitions to realize task-specific changes. RecPo maintains a procedure knowledge base of skill-induced transitions, with each view exposing a reusable factor and preserving local skill connectivity. At deployment, it interprets task specifications through the same views and resolves the resulting compositional queries over the stored relations to bind skills for execution. On long-horizon tasks in an extended Franka Kitchen benchmark, RecPo achieves 91.9% ordered completion with 1.0 ms of task inference per episode across varying procedure support and task-record sparsity. Real-robot studies further demonstrate adaptation through local memory edits without task-specific retraining.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 RecPo，用多种 procedure view 以任务无关方式表示技能，维护技能引发的转移知识库，并在部署时把任务与过程规格解析为组合查询，绑定出可执行技能序列；在 Franka Kitchen 长程任务上以每回合约 1 ms 推理取得 91.9% 有序完成率，实机可通过局部记忆编辑适配新任务而无需重训。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「因子化视图＋在存储关系上做组合查询＋局部记忆编辑」的状态抽象与稀疏监督下绑定组合思路，可能为 latent 推理状态的可重组、任务条件绑定及低成本计算提供概念类比，但属机器人技能领域、无视觉推理证据，可供核查线索较少。
